name: Scorpius
introduction: is the Scorpion, one of the few constellations that actually look like their name: a bright red heart, a curving body and a raised stinger. In myth, the scorpion killed Orion, so the two were placed on opposite sides of the sky; as Scorpius rises, Orion sets. It is a constellation of the zodiac, best seen in southern winter and northern summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Many of the blue-white stars of Scorpius are siblings. They belong to the Scorpius–Centaurus association, the nearest region of recent massive star formation to the Sun, about 400 to 500 light-years away. Its youngest group, Upper Scorpius, is only about ten million years old. Supernova explosions from this family helped blow out the [Local Bubble](id:local-bubble), the hot, thin cavity in which the Sun now sits.

At its heart is [Antares](hip:80763), a red supergiant whose radius is more than three times the distance from the Earth to the Sun. If it replaced the Sun, its surface would extend beyond the orbit of Mars.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Antares](hip:80763) means “rival of Mars”: its red color resembles the planet, which sometimes passes nearby. About 550 light-years away, it has a hot blue companion that is easily lost in its glare.

The stinger is marked by [Shaula](hip:85927), one of the brightest stars in the sky, and its neighbors [Sargas](hip:86228), [Kappa Scorpii](hip:86670) and [Iota¹ Scorpii](hip:87073). [Dschubba](hip:78401), in the scorpion’s head, surprised astronomers in 2000 when it began spinning off a disk of gas and brightened noticeably. [Xamidimura](hip:82514) is an eclipsing binary, and [Zeta¹ Scorpii](hip:82671), more than 5,000 light-years away, is a blue hypergiant, among the most luminous stars known in our galaxy.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Around Antares, dust reflects starlight into clouds of color, including the [Antares Nebula](id:ic-4606) and the [Blue Horsehead Nebula](id:ic-4592).

Nearby lie the globular cluster M4, one of the nearest to Earth, just west of Antares; the open clusters M6 and M7 near the stinger; and Scorpius X-1, discovered in 1962 as the first X-ray source outside the Solar System.
